To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AFM nanoindentations were applied to investigate the mechanical properties of living human hepatocellular carcinomas treated with fullerenols for 24,48 and 72 hours.
AFM nanoindenting is an effective method to evaluate the effects on cancer cells of anticancer agents and to provide insight into the cancer treatment.
we have derived both Young’s modulus (E) and work of adhesions (Wadh) of biological cells (Hepatocellular carcinoma) using AFM nanoindentations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of work of adhesions of human hepatocellular cancer cells by AFM nano-indentation.
the mechanical properties of living cells and the effects of anticancer agents on cell mechanical properties, which can provide a novel method for cancer diagnosis and therapy.
the investigation of the work of adhesive forces and Young’s modulus for biological cells (human carcinoma) by JKR contact model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the JKR model can be used for the analysis of adhesion phenomenon of biological cells and the obtained work of adhesion is a useful parameter to evaluate the effect of anticancer agents on biological cells.
the JKR model is more suitable than Hertz model for fitting the force-displacement curves of biological cells.
the work of adhesions of the cells can be a more sensitive parameter for the evaluation of the anticancer effects of fullerenols than elastic modulus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the work of adhesions of biological cells could be determined by AFM nanoindention and the obtained results would be helpful to evaluate the effect of fullerenol on cancer cells.

the JKR contact model is suitable to describe the mechanical properties of biological cells and the work of adheasion is a useful parameter to evaluate the effects and the mechanisms of fullerenol on cancer cells.

we have developed an AFM-based method for investigation of mechanical properties of cancer cells under fullerenol treatments, and the results show that the work of adhesions can provide more information than elastic modulus in the investigation of cancer progression in the treatments of anticancer agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AFM nanoindentations can be a useful tool for studying the biomechanical properties and adhesion phenomena of biological cells.
the JKR contact model can provide better results for the analysis of the adhesion of biological cells.
the JKR model can be used to determine the elastic modulus and work-of-adhesion of biological cells.
